messages.text: Arteta explains reaction to Dowman red card amid criticism

metadata.summary: Mikel Arteta has explained his reaction to Max Dowman as the 16-year-old went down the tunnel after being sent off in Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.
metadata.content: Max Dowman red card: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta explains his reaction to 16-year-old after sending off in Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Max Dowman red card: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta explains his reaction to 16-year-old after sending off in Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town Max Dowman was sent off in Arsenal's defeat to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup and Mikel Arteta appeared to say something to the 16-year-old as he went down the tunnel; that drew criticism from Paul Merson but Arteta has explained what he said to the 16-year-old Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Wednesday 28 October 2026 07:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson was critical of Mikel Arteta's reaction to Max Dowman being sent off Mikel Arteta has explained his reaction to Max Dowman as the 16-year-old went down the tunnel after being sent off in Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town. Moments before Arsenal exited the competition on penalties to the League Two side, Dowman was sent off for violent conduct for kicking out at Harrison Neal after the Fleetwood defender's strong challenge on the teenager. As Dowman headed towards the tunnel and past the dugouts, Arteta leaned in and said something to the teenager, which Paul Merson criticised, saying the Arsenal manager should have put an arm around him. metadata.content: New York Knicks 111-97 Detroit Pistons: Reigning champions Knicks beat Pistons for first win of the season | Basketball News | Sky Sports Home Sports Football F1 Cricket Rugby Union Rugby League Golf Boxing NFL Tennis NBA Racing Darts Netball MMA More Sports Scores Football F1 Cricket Rugby Union Rugby League Golf NFL Tennis Watch Sky Bet More Podcasts Live on Sky Get Sky Sports Sky Sports App Sky Sports with no contract Kick It Out British South Asians in Football Watch Sky Sports Basketball News News News Fixtures/Results Rankings Basketball on Sky Photos Sky Bet New York Knicks 111-97 Detroit Pistons: Reigning champions Knicks beat Pistons for first win of the season Reigning champions the New York Knicks had lost their first three games of the new season but rallied to beat the Detroit Pistons 111-97; Coach Mike Brown said: "We're more than capable if we put our minds to it, and that's what we've got to continue to try to build off" Last Updated: 28/10/26 7:53am New York Knicks' Jalen Brunson has begun to break out of his early-season slump (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II) NBA's reigning champions, the New York Knicks, secured their first win of the season when they came back to beat the Detroit Pistons 111-97. Down by 13 points after one quarter, they outscored the Pistons 63-25 across the next two, putting the kind of numbers on the scoreboard they did repeatedly during their march to the NBA championship. messages.text: Rising star Domingos hopes to mastermind England's World Cup retention

metadata.summary: Just 18 months ago, Luis Domingos had not played Wheelchair Rugby League and now he heads to Australia with the hope of defending a world title with England.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: Meet England wheelchair's rising basketball star Luis Domingos who wants to help the side keep hold of their title | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Rugby League World Cup: Meet England wheelchair's rising basketball star Luis Domingos who wants to help the side keep hold of their title England's wheelchair team head into the Rugby league World Cup as defending champions; Luis Domingos is one of the players tasked with keeping hold of the title; He had not played the sport even two years ago but has used his basketball skills to help his rapid rise Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Wednesday 28 October 2026 06:51, UK Image: England Wheelchair Rugby League player Luis Domingos has had a rapid rise in the sport he picked up less than two years ago Just 18 months ago, Luis Domingos had not played Wheelchair Rugby League and now he heads to Australia with the hope of defending a world title with England. Despite picking up the sport not too long ago, it is not the first time that Domingos has made his mark on the international stage. Domingos used to represent Portugal in wheelchair basketball and was professional in the sport. However, to finish his studies at university, he left wheelchair basketball. Then he attended a wheelchair rugby league training session and the rest, they say, is history.
